findings.message:
[P1] Retained closed PR is dropped without a retired marker

The new branch retains `target.pr` but never records it in `target.retiredOwnPr`, and `recoverClosedExistingHead` then calls `createPullRequestFor` with only `target.pr: null` (loop-existing-head-continuation.ts:190-193). That drops the closed PR number before the replacement's `pullRequestIntentKey` and `guardCiMinuteEffect` effect are built, so `publicationAfter` is undefined and the replacement reuses the original head's `pr_open` effect digest. With an active CI-minute policy, the closed original PR resolves as `not_applied` while its reservation is already settled, so `guardCiMinuteEffect` defers instead of admitting the replacement and the row still cannot republish; repeated replacements also reuse a stale marker. The same branch in `requestReviewFor` (loop-review-request.ts:130-132) has the identical issue.

src/repair/loop-review-observation.ts:166-171

summary: The guard now admits retired closed-publication rows and tests cover the recovery, but the retained-PR path drops the closed PR number before rebuilding the replacement publication identity, so CI-minute admission can still block the republish.

evidence: The guard now reads `retiredOwnPr` and admits `pr === null` / `intent === null` records when a closed-publication marker exists (loop-existing-head-continuation.ts:112-123).
observeReview and requestReviewFor keep the closed PR through the work step so the live branch can be re-verified before a replacement is opened.
New regression tests cover observation and request retirement, review-intent recovery, restart reconciliation, and branch-mismatch refusal in tests/repair/loop-closed-existing-head_test.ts.
In the new tests the live-branch retired row opens a replacement PR and returns to review without a model start.
